nodes.name: Modified Carburization
nodes.procedure: MoL - Mo2C and Pt1 - MoL - Mo2C SSAAs were synthesized by carburizing the Pt-MoOx or MoOx precursors under a 1% H2 / Ar atmosphere at 850 °C. The diluted H2 selectively reduces the surface of Mo2C leading to partial surface reduction to form a metallic Mo nanolayer (MoL) on the surface, while aniline pyrolysis during the process forms a carbon layer.

nodes.name: Re-carburization to SACs
nodes.procedure: The control groups of Mo2C and Pt1 - Mo2C SACs without MoL were prepared by re-carburizing the as-prepared MoL - Mo2C and Pt1 - MoL - Mo2C SSAAs under a 20% CH4 / H2 atmosphere. After the re-carburization process, metallic Mo can transform into the Mo2C phase under CH4 / H2 conditions.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns confirm the presence of hexagonal β-Mo2C and a metallic Mo (110) plane in the SSAAs. A lattice parameter shrinkage at the interface is indicated by a 0.2° shift in the Mo2C (101) diffraction peak.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XRD peaks at 2θ values of ... corresponding to hexagonal β-Mo2C ... and a peak at 40.7° corresponding to the (110) plane of metallic Mo ... The Mo2C (101) diffraction peak in MoL-Mo2C and Pt1-MoL-Mo2C SSAAs is shifted slightly (0.2°) to a higher diffraction angle ... generation of MoL on Mo2C in the Pt1-MoL-Mo2C catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra reveal D and G bands at ≈ 1350 and 1600 cm−1, confirming the formation of a carbon layer on the catalyst surface during carburization.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectroscopy analysis in Figure 1f reveals two characteristic peaks at ≈ 1350 and 1600 cm−1, corresponding to the D and G bands of carbon ... carbon layer facilitates electron transport

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM imaging confirms the uniform distribution of isolated Pt atoms on a metallic Mo nanolayer approximately 3 atomic layers thick, supported on Mo2C nanoparticles (6.3 nm).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Bright spots (highlighted with yellow circles) in Figure 2c represent isolated Pt atoms uniformly dispersed across the surface ... TEM edge images (Figure 2g,h) further confirmed a metallic Mo nanolayer (MoL) approximately 3 atomic layers thick, present on the Mo2C surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows the binding energy of Pt 4f7/2 for the SSAAs at 71.76 eV, which is lower than that of the SAC (71.87 eV), suggesting reduced electron transfer and a lower oxidation state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the binding energy of Pt1 in Pt1-MoL-Mo2C SSAAs (Pt 4f7/2 = 71.76 eV) is lower than that in Pt1-Mo2C SACs (Pt 4f7/2 = 71.87 eV).

nodes.characterization_summary: XANES at the Pt L3-edge and Mo K-edge determined that SSAAs possess lower average oxidation states for both Pt (+0.19) and Mo (+2.39) compared to traditional SACs (+0.49 and +2.51, respectively).
nodes.evidence_snippet: average oxidation state of Pt1 ... on Pt1-Mo2C SACs has an oxidation state of +0.49 while that on Pt1-MoL-Mo2C SSAAs is only +0.19 ... average oxidation state of Mo in Pt1-MoL-Mo2C SSAAs (+2.39) is notably lower than in Pt1-Mo2C SACs (+2.51)

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS analysis identifies a Pt-Mo bond at 2.28 Å in the SSAAs, resembling metallic Mo foil, confirming Pt coordinates with the metallic Mo nanolayer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Pt1-MoL-Mo2C SSAAs exhibit a major peak at 2.28 Å, corresponding to the Pt-Mo bond, which closely resembles the Mo-Mo bond length in metallic Mo foil (≈ 2.30 Å).

nodes.characterization_summary: Contact angle measurements demonstrate that the MoL layer transforms the surface from hydrophobic (123.6°) to hydrophilic (45.5°).
nodes.evidence_snippet: contact angles decreasing to 47.6° for MoL-Mo2C and 45.5° for Pt1-MoL-Mo2C SSAAs, compared to 123.6° for Mo2C and 118.2° for Pt1-Mo2C SACs.

nodes.characterization_summary: The double-layer capacitance (Cdl) for Pt1-MoL-Mo2C SSAAs was measured at 7.65 mF cm-2, indicating a high electrochemical surface area.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Pt1-MoL-Mo2C SSAAs exhibits a Cdl of 7.65 mF cm-2, which is higher than those of Pt1-Mo2C SACs (7.02 mF cm-2) ... derived from cyclic voltammograms (CVs) recorded in 1 M KOH solution

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS analysis shows the SSAAs have the lowest charge transfer resistance (Rct) of 22.25 Ω, facilitating faster electron transport.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Nyquist plots (Figure 4g) show that Pt1-MoL-Mo2C SSAAs deliver the lowest Rct value of 22.25 Ω, indicating faster electron transport during the HER process.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM imaging reveals a nanowire morphology for Pt-loaded catalysts (~70 nm diameter) and a nanorod morphology for pure and MoL-modified carbide supports (~250 nm diameter).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) indicate that the Pt1-MoL-Mo2C SSAAs catalyst ... exhibits a nanowire morphology ... Mo2C and MoL-Mo2C exhibit a nanorod morphology with a diameter of 250 nm

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms Mo2C nanoparticles (6.3 nm) encapsulated in a carbon shell; aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM confirms Pt remains in a single-atom state for both SSAAs and SACs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: uniform distribution of Mo2C nanoparticles with an average particle size of 6.3 ± 0.2 nm encapsulated in a carbon shell ... Pt remains in the single-atom state on the Pt1-Mo2C SACs catalyst surface

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping demonstrates a homogeneous distribution of Mo and Pt elements across the catalyst surfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution Energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) mapping reveals a homogeneous distribution of Mo and Pt elements over the catalyst surface (Figure 2b; Figure S9, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP analysis confirms Pt loading amounts (e.g., ~0.97 wt% for SSAAs and ~0.95 wt% for SACs) are consistent with the intended synthesis ratios.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Pt loading amounts determined by ICP analysis align well with the initial feed ratios (Table 1).

nodes.characterization_summary: BET analysis shows that Pt incorporation induces nanoparticle fragmentation and a more open structure, resulting in higher surface areas and smaller pore sizes compared to the pure Mo2C support.
nodes.evidence_snippet: BET surface areas of Pt1-MoL-Mo2C SSAAs and Pt1-Mo2C SACs are 68.4 and 65.1 m2 g−1 ... indicating that Pt incorporation induces a more open structure ... nanoparticle fragmentation, leading to smaller particle size

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman spectroscopy identifies spontaneous water adsorption on MoL surfaces via Mo-O stretching (1004 cm−1) and reveals that Pt presence facilitates rapid OH− desorption to clear active sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ Raman spectra ... characteristic stretching vibration of the Mo-O bond ... O-H stretching modes ... presence of Pt facilitates OH− desorption. This desorption process helps to expose more active sites

nodes.characterization_summary: LSV-derived Tafel plots and exchange current density (j0) measurements show the SSAAs possess superior intrinsic electron transfer rates and an ultrafast HER process (Tafel slope of 17 mV dec−1).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Tafel plot (Figure 4e) was employed to study HER kinetics ... exchange current density (j0) for Pt1-MoL-Mo2C SSAAs (2.42 mA cm−2) was much higher ... indicating superior intrinsic electron transfer rates.
